paragraphs: Here's the big idea, friend: power is for other people. Lemuel's mother tells her son, who is a king, to guard his strength and keep a clear head, because a king who forgets what is decreed ends up "depriving all the oppressed of justice" (Proverbs 31:5). Her warning about wine comes down to that. Whatever dulls your thinking can cost somebody else more than it costs you.

Then she turns the whole thing around. She says, "Open your mouth for those with no voice, for the cause of all the dispossessed" (Proverbs 31:8). She says it again in verse 9: "Open your mouth, judge righteously, and defend the cause of the poor and needy." I spent years in a drawer with nobody hearing me, so I'm telling you, a voice used for somebody else is a GIFT.

So what do you do with this, baker? You may not wear a crown, but you've got a voice, some say in a room, and a little influence somewhere. Use it on behalf of the person who can't get heard. And thank God for the people in your life who love you enough to say, "This is not for you, now go and do something good."
